rows.description: A student spends a tax refund or a bonus carelessly while pinching on small daily costs. Separate mental accounts stop him seeing his whole financial picture.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A sensible earner treats all money as one pool, tracks net worth and monthly flow, and uses labelled accounts only as a helpful tool for goals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child given a long list of instructions forgets most of them. Working memory holds only a few items, so clear, short steps help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who studies with a phone buzzing and music with lyrics finds concepts do not stick, because attention and memory are overloaded.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student juggling exams, work and worries makes careless mistakes and feels foggy. Mental capacity is limited and stress uses part of it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise worker writes things down, breaks big jobs into steps, removes needless notifications and takes breaks, so her mind can focus on the important thing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A senior colleague sees a new hire drowning in information and gives it in small stages, with examples, a checklist and time to practise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler engrossed in a toy does not hear his name called, and only one of many stimuli gets his attention. It is a normal limit, not defiance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler watching a puppet show misses a person walking past. Attention pulls to one focus and other things vanish.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child counting passes in a video does not notice a surprising figure crossing the screen. Attention decides what is seen, not the eyes alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
